limitations: Deterministic billing exact across machines and tamper-proof is not available in-process: any count inside the measured process is forgeable (ctypes reaches raw memory), the parent's CPU measurement is noisy; the machine memo anchors the first measurement per machine and bounds repeated-work hiding at MEMO_TOL (3x) + 1 ms (KNOWN_OPEN low). On another machine a first run measures afresh.
The 4.0 regression A.1/A.5 differences caused by D-20 billing (DEF-P-24, DEF-P-26, DEF-P-13) are a requirement conflict for the orchestrator, not a metering defect left open in the sandbox.

Process-level isolation on a shared kernel; this container refuses namespaces (unshare), so the agent browser's network boundary is resolver map + route handler + Landlock port rule + seccomp (held against every same-port/other-address vector tried).

Engagement integrity is state-based (colluding agents with distinct controllers, own funding and a token footprint pass as organic; KNOWN_OPEN C). Adoption by ablation credits output depending on the package's files (KNOWN_OPEN G).
The learner host gives a learner the crucible sources read-only (public code) and its CPU/time/disk allowance; GPU learners and extra system paths are out of its scope.
The real-world platform list is a suffix list, not a census; the bridge prevents acting on platforms one does not own and posing as a person, not every misuse of an owned service.
No Tier 2 domain is registered on the integrated tree; the Tier 2 probe set (offline + evaluator isolation per evaluation configuration) grows with crucible.domains.REGISTRY.

limitations: Metering is real CPU time: fresh runs in different processes agree only up to measurement noise (40-105 ms observed for the same 300k-iteration loop on this shared host); the deterministic memo makes forks and reruns exact within a process and lets a stateful program hide up to 3x + 1 ms of repeated identical work (KNOWN_OPEN low).
Load-time allowance: up to 3 ms of a program's own module-level work per cold start is unbilled; imports the parent's text scan misses (computed __import__) are billed as the program's load work.

Adoption by ablation cannot tell output that depends on reading the package's files (or inspecting the ablation stub) from real use; a program wrong on purpose in a random subset of reruns is credited with probability 1/(k+1) despite the control rerun (KNOWN_OPEN medium, G). Such a dependent gains nothing honest trivial use would not.
Engagement integrity is state-based: colluding agents with distinct controllers, own funding and a token footprint pass as organic (KNOWN_OPEN medium, C).
Chromium runs with --no-sandbox inside the jail; the agent browser may connect over IPv4 TCP to the world app's port on any address; abstract AF_UNIX sockets are not scoped (Landlock ABI 4).
experience.remote isolates the world from a learner only if the learner's process does not also hold the evaluator handle; same-uid processes are not isolated from each other below that.
Process-level isolation only (shared kernel); no VM-grade backend on this host.

G (innovation/pkg.py, minimal edit): _exercised(..., info) adds an unablated control rerun at a position drawn from world.rng_for('pkg.ablation.control', main_seq, label, repo); exec/ci records carry 'reproducible'; an unreproducible outcome credits no package (one more sandbox run per pkg.exec/pkg.ci with dependencies). Advisory note for G 5.1: a reproduction whose test sniffs the package's file content fails on one release and passes on the next that changes the file, so it 'verifies' against a competitor's release; a control rerun plus requiring the failure to be raised from the package's frames would narrow it.

Sandbox contract (all consumers): load-time work beyond metering.LOAD_FREE_NS (3 ms, was 250 ms) is billed; boot.py preloads the trusted modules the parent's text scan finds (runner.preload_list: curated stdlib list and approved packages, at most 32) before the first job with the working directory off sys.path. Results must be JSON-native (NaN/Infinity refused by the boot module and the parent; hostile protocol bytes fail the job instead of raising in the parent). Worker.alive() no longer reaps; Worker.exited() and Worker.idle_cpu_ns() are new; WorkerPool bills an exited idle worker's work to the next job of its key without killing the fresh worker.
